subject: chemistry
title: Alloys
key_idea: In a pure metal the layers of atoms slide easily, so it is soft. An alloy has atoms of different sizes, which distort the layers so they cannot easily slide. Alloys are harder, and each is chosen for the properties its use needs.

sections.heading: Why alloys are harder than pure metals

blocks.text: An alloy is a mixture of a metal with other elements, usually other metals. This section explains why alloys are harder.

items.meaning: A mixture of a metal with other elements, usually other metals.

items: In a pure metal the atoms are all the same size and are arranged in regular layers.
The layers can slide over each other, so a pure metal can be bent and shaped. It is also soft.
In an alloy the atoms are of different sizes.
The different sized atoms distort the layers, so the layers cannot easily slide over each other.
So an alloy is harder and stronger than the pure metal.

diagram.alt: A pure metal compared with an alloy.
items: Pure metal
Alloy
Pure metals are too soft for many uses.
An alloy has atoms of different sizes, which distort the layers.
Distorted layers cannot easily slide, so an alloy is harder.

sections.heading: Common alloys and their uses (Separate science)

blocks.text: Most metals in everyday use are alloys. Each alloy is made for the properties its use needs.

rows: Used for bells, statues and ship propellers.
Strong and hard wearing. Used for musical instruments and plug pins.
Gold with silver, copper and zinc
Harder than pure gold, and cheaper.
Iron with a high amount of carbon
Iron with a low amount of carbon
Aluminium alloys, such as magnalium (aluminium and magnesium)
Low density. Used for aircraft parts.

items: The proportion of gold in an alloy is measured in carats.
24 carat is pure gold (100%).
18 carat is 75% gold.

blocks.label: Percentage of gold in an alloy
where: carats = the carat value of the alloy

blocks.label: Mass of gold in an object
blocks.formula: mass of gold = (percentage of gold ÷ 100) × mass of object

items: Bronze is copper and tin. Brass is copper and zinc.
Steels are iron with carbon. More carbon makes steel stronger but more brittle.
24 carat is 100% gold. Carat ÷ 24 × 100 gives the percentage.

blocks.text: To choose a metal for a use, match its properties to what the use needs. Compare the data given in the question.

items: Aluminium is used for cooking foil. It is malleable and has low toxicity.
Copper is used for water pipes and electrical wires. It is unreactive and a good conductor of electricity.
Gold is used for jewellery and electronic contacts. It is unreactive, does not corrode and is a good conductor.
Gold alloys are harder and cheaper than pure gold.
Aluminium alloys have low density and are stronger than pure aluminium, so they suit aircraft parts.
Brass is strong and hard wearing, so it suits plug pins.
Stainless steel is hard and resists corrosion.

worked_example.question:
Pure iron is too soft for many uses.

Explain why mixing iron with other metals makes alloys which are harder than pure iron.
answer_points: The alloy has atoms of different sizes.
So the layers of atoms are distorted.
So the layers cannot easily slide over each other.
worked_example.tip: Ions are allowed for atoms throughout.

worked_example.question:
Aluminium alloys are used instead of pure aluminium in aircraft manufacture.

Explain, in terms of the arrangement of metal particles, why aluminium alloys are stronger than pure aluminium.
answer_points: In an alloy the atoms are different sizes (in pure aluminium they are all the same size).
In pure aluminium the layers of atoms easily slide over each other.
In an alloy the layers of atoms cannot easily slide over each other.

worked_example.question:
Magnalium is an alloy of aluminium and magnesium.

The table shows some information about aluminium, magnesium and magnalium.

| | Density (g / cm3) | Relative strength | Resistance to corrosion |
| Aluminium | 2.7 | low | high |
| Magnesium | 1.7 | low | low |
| Magnalium | 2.0 | high | very high |

Magnalium is used to make aircraft parts.

Explain why magnalium is used to make aircraft parts rather than pure aluminium or pure magnesium.

Use the information in the table.
answer_points: Magnalium has a lower density than pure aluminium.
Magnalium is stronger than aluminium or magnesium.
Magnalium has a higher resistance to corrosion than aluminium or magnesium.
worked_example.tip: Each point must be a comparison, not just a quoted value.
